proposals.before: 3.1 Let $E:=\{x:m(\theta,x)=\infty\}$, measurable by step 2.1. For each positive integer $n$, $n\mathbf1_E\le m(\theta,\cdot)$, so [F6] and step 1.2 give $n\nu(E)\le1$. Since this holds for every $n$, [F7] forces $\nu(E)=0$. If $0<m(\theta,x)<\infty$, division by that scalar and the definition of $m$ give $\int q(z\mid\theta,x)\,\mu(dz)=m(\theta,x)/m(\theta,x)=1$. The valid-fibre set $V=m^{-1}((0,\infty))$ is measurable by step 2.1 and [F8]. For measurability, define $\rho:[0,\infty]\to[0,\infty]$ by $\rho(t)=1/t$ for finite $t>0$ and $\rho(0)=\rho(+\infty)=0$. For $a<0$, $\{\rho>a\}=[0,\infty]$; for $a=0$ it is $(0,\infty)$; and for $a>0$ it is $(0,1/a)$. These sets are Borel by [F8], so [F9] makes $\rho$ Borel. By [F10], $\rho\circ m$ is measurable on $\Theta\times\mathsf X$. Pulling it back along the measurable coordinate projection from the finite product space, which is measurable by [F12], gives a product-measurable function; multiplying by $p$ preserves measurability by [F11]. This product restricts to $q=p/m$ on $V\times\mathsf Z$, so $q$ is measurable on the valid-fibre set. [F1, F6, F7, F8, F9, F10, F11, F12, step 2.1, step 1.2, algebra]
